{{See also|Dungeons}} {{Infobox/Generic |image = File:Mort Skull.png }} The '''Catacombs''' are the first [[Dungeons|Dungeon]] in SkyBlock. It can be accessed through speaking to {{NPCSprite|Mort}} in the {{Zone|Catacombs Entrance}} or {{Zone|Dungeon Hub}}. Players are, by default, required to be in a party of {{Green|2}}-{{Green|5}} [[Player|players]] in order to join the Catacombs. {{Gamemode|Bingo}} profiles are exempt from the normal party requirement. Giving {{NPCSprite|Mort}} a {{Item|Saul's Recommendation}} from {{NPCSprite|Adventurer Saul}} also allows players to enter the Catacombs on their own. You can set up your own party and invite your friends to join, or you can set up a party through the '''Party Finder''', where you can select different options and requirements for people to join your party. == Overview == * The '''Catacombs''' are a series of floors, each with interconnecting [[Catacombs Rooms|rooms]] filled with [[Dungeon Mobs|mobs]], [[Dungeon Secrets|secrets]], [[Dungeon Traps|traps]], and [[Dungeon Puzzle|puzzles]]. * The main goal of a run is to progress through the floor, defeat {{NPCSprite|The Watcher}}, and then defeat the {{Boss}}. * After killing all mobs in a room that have a {{Yellow|✯}} star in their nametag, the room is marked as cleared and will drop: ** a {{Item|Blessing}} and/or a {{Item|Superboom TNT}}; ** a {{Item|Wither Key}}, which unlocks more sections of the floor. The {{Item|Blood Key}} is dropped when killing all {{Yellow|✯}} mobs in the last room before the [[The Watcher|Blood Room]] and will unlock said room, where {{NPCSprite|The Watcher}} summons [[The Watcher's Undeads|Undeads]] that must be killed in order to progress to the {{Boss}} room. === Rules === While in the '''Catacombs''', several mechanics are changed or disabled: * [[Potions|Potion]] effects from outside the Catacombs are paused while inside. * Only one [[Potions|potion]] may be consumed or splashed per run, with the exception of {{Item|Stamina Potion|text=Stamina}}, {{Item|Healing Potion|text=Healing}}, and {{Item|Mana Potion}}s. {{Item|God Potion}}s cannot be consumed. ** Players can receive effects from multiple potions if they are splashed or consumed simultaneously. * Players may not access the [[Auction House]], [[Bazaar]], [[The Hex|Hex]], or an [[Anvil]], even while under the effect of a {{Item|Booster Cookie}}. * Players may not warp to private islands. * Players may not ride on mounts, like the {{Item|Armadillo Pet|text=Armadillo}} or {{Item|Rock Pet}}. * Every hit on an enemy restores {{Stat|Mana|5 + 1% of the player's maximum}}. This applies to melee attacks, bow hits, and the {{AN|Mage Staff}} passive of the [[Mage]] class. ** This does not apply to item abilities, such as {{AN|Guided Bat}} from the {{Item|Spirit Sceptre}}, or class abilities, such as {{AN|Explosive Shot}}. * All {{Stat|spd}} above {{Stat|spd|100}} is multiplied by {{Red|0.67}}. * [[Arrows]] deal reduced knockback and do not respect invincibility frames. * {{Stat|dmg}} against bosses is reduced above certain thresholds, depending on the boss. * {{Ench|Dragon Tracer}} is explicitly disabled, [[healing]] from {{Ench|Vampirism}} is reduced by {{Red|10x}}, and slowness from {{Ench|Venomous}} is greatly reduced. * The [[Purse]] is not displayed, and bonuses from items that scale with coins in the Purse do not work. * All purchases from [[Dungeon Reward Chest]]s or NPCs take coins directly from your [[Bank]]. === Classes === {{Main|Classes}} Players can choose one of five [[Classes]]: '''Berserk''', '''Archer''', '''Mage''', '''Tank''', and '''Healer'''. Each class serves a different purpose and has their own abilities, class passives, and ghost abilities. They are more effective if only one of each are present in a party, although multiple players can choose the same class if they wish. * '''Berserks''' prioritize dealing as much melee {{Stat|dmg}} as possible. * '''Archers''' prioritize dealing as much ranged {{Stat|dmg}} with a [[Bows|bow]] as possible. * '''Mages''' prioritize using their item abilities to deal as much magic damage as possible. ** A sub-sect of Mage, known as '''Left-Click Mage''', uses their {{AN|Mage Staff}} passive to deal high amounts of melee {{Stat|dmg}}. * '''Tanks''' prioritize staying near their teammates and diverting as much {{Stat|dmg}} as possible to themselves. * '''Healers''' prioritize providing [[healing]] and support to their teammates and themselves. === Ghosts === {{Main|Ghosts}} When a player loses all their {{Stat|hp}} in the '''Catacombs''', they do not die traditionally. Instead, they turn into a '''Ghost''' and function as a spectator with unique abilities and limited access to the [[SkyBlock Menu]]. Dying does not remove coins held in the [[Purse]] or degrade the {{Item|Piggy Bank}}, regardless of whether a {{Item|Booster Cookie}} is active. Ghosts can be revived during the run. If a player leaves a Catacombs run and rejoins it, they can return as a Ghost and be revived. Ghosts can only interact with the environment through their abilities: these abilities depend on their chosen [[Classes|Class]], and are listed below. {| class="wikitable" ! Class !! Name !! Has a {{Green|20s}} cooldown. |} == Floors == The '''Catacombs''' has {{Green|7}} floors and {{Green|1}} entrance: beating a floor unlocks the one succeeding it. Defeating {{MobSprite|Necron}}, the boss of [[The Catacombs - Floor VII]], unlocks '''Master Mode''', a harder version of the Catacombs will be available. {{/Floors}} == Rooms and Exploration == === Generation === A Catacombs floor consists of connected rooms. Special rooms generate in {{Aqua|1x1}} spaces, while Standard Rooms can generate in {{Aqua|1x1}}, {{Aqua|1x2}}, {{Aqua|1x3}}, {{Aqua|1x4}}, {{Aqua|2x2}}, or {{Aqua|L-shaped}}{{Footnote|{{Aqua|L-shaped}} refers to a {{Aqua|2x2}} space with one {{Aqua|1x1}} space removed.}} spaces. The path to the {{Red|Blood Room}} is guarded by a series of {{Dark Gray|Wither Doors}} and ends at the {{Red|Blood Door}}. The {{Pink|Fairy Room}} always generates along this path. At least {{Green|2}} {{DarkPurple|Puzzle Rooms}} generate in a floor. [[Dungeon Mobs]] spawn in Standard Rooms at predetermined locations, with some rooms also having predetermined mob types. [[Dungeon Secrets]] also appear in predetermined locations. Finding a Secret grants loot or a team-wide {{Item|Blessing}} and adds {{Green|+1}} to the [[Dungeon Score|Exploration Score]]{{Footnote|A special case is the {{MobSprite|Mimic}}.}}. === Room Types === There are several different rooms in the Catacombs, organized by color: {| class="wikitable" ! Room !! Description |- ! {{DarkGreen|Starter Room}} | The '''Starter Room''' is the room where the Dungeon begins: players can ready up and change their class in this room before the run starts. {{NPCSprite|Mort}} can be found here, and he gives players a {{Item|Dungeon Orb}} on lower floors. |- ! Standard Room | Each Dungeon run mostly consists of '''Standard Rooms'''. They contain a multitude of mobs and secrets: some mobs will have a yellow star next to their names, marking them as unique. When all unique mobs, or a miniboss, are killed, they will drop an item and mark the room as complete: two of these are guaranteed to be a {{Item|Wither Key}}, and one of these is guaranteed to be a {{Item|Blood Key}}. |- ! {{DarkPurple|Puzzle Room}} | The '''Puzzle Room''' contains a [[Catacombs Puzzle Rooms|Puzzle]] that must be completed for the room to be marked as completed. Some can be failed, and others cannot: they can be reset with an {{Item|Architect's First Draft}}. |- ! {{Yellow|Miniboss Room}} | The '''Miniboss Room''' contains a random [[Minibosses|Miniboss]]: killing them will mark the room as complete. The miniboss can be a {{MobSprite|Angry Archaeologist}}, {{MobSprite|Lost Adventurer}}, {{MobSprite|King Midas}}, {{MobSprite|Shadow Assassin}}, or {{MobSprite|Frozen Adventurer}}. |- ! {{Gold|Trap Room}} | The '''Trap Room''' consists of several traps and obstacles that must be overcome. They contain several [[Dungeon Secrets|secrets]] that must be all completed in order to mark the room as complete. Trap Rooms can generate from [[The Catacombs - Floor III|Floor III]] through [[The Catacombs - Floor VII|Floor VII]], including their [[Master Mode]] counterparts. |- ! {{Pink|Fairy Room}} | The '''Fairy Room''' consists of a large tree in the middle, with several {{MobSprite|Fairy;Fairies}} surrounding it that drop a {{Item|Revive Stone}} when killed. A healing pool can be found near the tree. Killing a Fairy here revives a dead player, and a dead player can also kill one to revive themselves. |- ! {{Red|Blood Room}} | The '''Blood Room''' is the final room that must be completed before the boss room can be accessed. {{NPCSprite|The Watcher}} will summon lots of Undead that must be all killed in order for the room to be marked as completed: on higher floors, they will receive modifiers and some will take the appearance of previous bosses, like {{NPCSprite|Bonzo}}, {{NPCSprite|Scarf}}, the {{MobSprite|Spirit Bear}}, or [[Sadan|Sadan's Giants]]. |} === Magical Map === {{Main|Magical Map}} The {{Item|Magical Map}} replaces the [[SkyBlock Menu]] while in the main section of a Catacombs floor and shows the layout of the floor, player locations, and room completion status. Entering the {{Boss}} room restores the normal [[SkyBlock Menu]]. The map uses the following indicators: * {{mctxt|white|?}} on a {{Gray|gray background}}: the room has not been explored. * ''{{Gray|Nothing}}'': the room is uncleared. * {{mctxt|c|✘}}: the room has been failed. * {{mctxt|f|✔}}: the room has been cleared and at least {{Green|1}} Secret remains undiscovered. * {{mctxt|2|✔}}: the room has been cleared and all of its Secrets have been discovered. Pressing {{Keypress|Right Click}} or {{Keypress|Left Click}} while holding the map runs /sbmenu. == Exploration and Rewards == Dungeon loot is obtained from [[Dungeon Secrets|Secrets]], drops from [[Dungeon Mobs]], and [[Dungeon Reward Chest]]s. === Finishing a Run === A Catacombs run ends when one of the following occurs: * The {{Boss}} is defeated. * All players in the run have either died and become [[Ghosts]] or left the run. * {{Green|60}} minutes pass without defeating the {{Boss}}. Players do not need to complete every room or defeat every mob to complete a run. === Dungeon Score === {{Main|Dungeon Score}} '''Dungeon Score''' is a value comprised of four categories: '''Skill''', or the number of deaths and [[Dungeon Puzzle Rooms|puzzles]] failed in a run; '''Exploration''', or the percentage of the floor completed and the number of [[Dungeon Secrets|secrets]] completed; '''Speed''', or the time taken to complete a run; and '''Bonus''', which varies depending on the floor and active modifiers, like {{NPCSprite|Paul}}'s {{AN|EZPZ}} perk. * '''0-99''' Score grants a '''{{Red|D}}'''. * '''100-159''' Score grants a '''{{Blue|C}}'''. * '''160-229''' Score grants a '''{{DarkPurple|B}}'''. * '''230-269.4''' Score grants a '''{{DarkGreen|A}}'''. * '''270-299''' Score grants a '''{{Gold|S}}'''. * '''≥300''' Score grants a '''{{Gold|S+}}'''. For more in-depth calculations, see [[Dungeon Score]]. === Dungeon Reward Chests === {{Main|Dungeon Reward Chest}} * When a floor is successfully cleared, player(s) can spend {{coins}} to unlock different tiers of '''Dungeon Reward Chests''', with each tier increasing in price and quality of loot. * The total Score achieved at the end of a Dungeon run dictates which [[Dungeon Reward Chest]]s are unlocked. Completion of the floor unlocks the '''Wood''', '''Gold''', and '''Diamond''' chests; an '''{{DarkGreen|A}}''' unlocks the '''Emerald''' chest; an '''{{Gold|S}}''' unlocks the '''Obsidian''' chest, and an '''{{Gold|S+}}''' unlocks the '''Bedrock''' chest while on [[The Catacombs - Floor V|Floor V]] or higher. While on [[The Catacombs - Floor VII]], you unlock an additional chest per phase of the boss fight completed.{{ConfirmationNeeded}} * When obtaining an item classified as an {{Pink|'''RNG Drop'''}}, the following dialogue is displayed: :{{Dialogue| &d&l----------------------------------- &d&lRNG DROP! &7 &ejust found a &6&e! &d&l----------------------------------- }} :*Items classified as {{Pink|'''RNG Drops'''}} include: :** {{Item|Livid Dagger}}{{Confirm}} :** {{Item|Shadow Fury}}{{Confirm}} :** {{Item|Last Breath}}{{Confirm}} :** {{Item|Giant's Sword}} :** {{Item|Fel Skull}}{{Confirm}} :** {{Item|Precursor Eye}}{{Confirm}} :** {{Item|Necron's Handle}} :** {{Item|Implosion}} :** {{Item|Wither Shield}} :** {{Item|Shadow Warp}} == Dungeonizing and Essence == {{Main|Essence}} Items used in the Catacombs can be either normal items or '''Dungeon items'''. Normal items do not have a {{mctxt||DUNGEON}} tag in their item type, while Dungeon items do. Some normal items can be converted into Dungeon items using [[Essence]], a process commonly called ''dungeonizing''. '''Essence''' is a currency used in the Catacombs that can be spent on upgrades at various NPCs, used to upgrade items, and convert items to '''Dungeon items'''. Dungeon items generally receive increased stats while in the Catacombs. The stat boosts depend on your {{Skill|Catacombs}} level, the number of [[Star Upgrades]] the item has, and the number of {{Item|Master Star}}s applied. If a [[Slayer]] item is converted into a Dungeon item, it can be used inside the Catacombs without meeting its Slayer level requirement. Most Dungeon items still require a certain {{Skill|Catacombs}} level. Gear dropped by mobs also uses the entry requirement of the floor it dropped on while inside that Dungeon instance. For example, a {{Item|Zombie Knight Chestplate}} dropped from {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor VII}} requires {{Skill|Catacombs|14}} normally, but {{Skill|Catacombs|24}} while inside the Catacombs. Standard [[Star Upgrades]] can be obtained on a variety of items that are not limited to being Catacombs-exclusive; however, {{Item|Master Star}}s can only be applied to Dungeon items. === Stat Bonuses === The stat bonuses from your {{Skill|Catacombs}} level and Star Upgrades are calculated separately and stack additively on top of the final state increase, only modifying the stats of the item itself. While in the Catacombs, each Star Upgrade grants a {{Green|+10%}} stat boost, adding up to a total stat boost of {{Green|+50%}}; each Master Star grants a {{Green|+5%}} stat boost on top of the initial increase, totaling to a {{Green|+75%}} increase in stats across the board. [[General's Medallion]] additionally grants a {{Green|+1%}} stat boost per digit, up to {{Green|+5%}}. Example: Catacombs 27 {{Green|[+255%]}} + 5 stars {{Green|[+50%]}} + 2 Master Stars {{Green|[+10%]}} + 1000 Secret Counter (4 Digits) {{Green|[+4%]}} = {{Green|+319%}}, while in Master Mode. This boost multiplies eligible stats by (100% + 319%)×. Some [[Stats]] are not boosted by every source, such as {{Stat|Attack Speed}}, {{Stat|Crit Chance}}, and {{Stat|Ability Damage}}. These stats do not receive the {{Skill|Catacombs}} Level stat boost, but can receive [[Star Upgrades|Stars]], {{Item|Master Star}}s, and [[General's Medallion]] digits boosts. {| class="wikitable centertext mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ Stats affected on Dungeon items ! There are up to {{Green|10}} possible 'tiers' of base stats, dependent on the floor the item was dropped on. {| class="wikitable" ! rowspan="2" | Tier ! colspan="2" | Floor |- ! {{aqua|"Normal" Mode}} ! {{red|Master Mode}} |- ! rowspan="2" class="ct" | 1 | {{Item|The Catacombs - Entrance}} | {{bc}} |- | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor I}} | {{bc}} |- ! class="ct" | 2 | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor II}} | {{bc}} |- ! class="ct" | 3 | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor III}} | {{bc}} |- ! class="ct" | 4 | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor IV}} | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor I (Master Mode)}} |- ! class="ct" | 5 | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor V}} | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor II (Master Mode)}} |- ! class="ct" | 6 | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor VI}} | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor III (Master Mode)}} |- ! class="ct" | 7 | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor VII}} | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor IV (Master Mode)}} |- ! class="ct" | 8 | {{bc}} | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor V (Master Mode)}} |- ! class="ct" | 9 | {{bc}} | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor VI (Master Mode)}} |- ! class="ct" | 10 | {{bc}} | {{Item|The Catacombs - Floor VII (Master Mode)}} |} The bonus stats of dropped items can reach up to a {{Green|+50%}} increase, which will result in its [[Rarity]] being upgraded. == Dungeoneering == {{Main|Dungeoneering}} {{Skill|Dungeoneering}} is a [[Skills|Skill]] that is leveled up through completing runs of the Catacombs. As players complete or fail Dungeon runs, they will increment {{Skill|Catacombs}} XP and eventually upgrade their {{Skill|Catacombs}} skill. Each level grants increased {{Stat|hp}} and {{SBXP}}, and grants a multiplicative stat multiplier on Dungeon items of up to {{Green|+485%}}. Additionally, the first {{Green|5}} completions each day award a {{Green|40%}} bonus to {{Skill|Catacombs}} XP. Failed runs do not count towards this bonus. == Trivia == *{{NPCSprite|The Professor}} was referred to as '''Oak''' on the [[Alpha Hypixel Network]].https://ibb.co/NCQp6f3https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3C3seezNuYg&t=12 **This was a reference to [[Bulb:Professor_Oak|Professor Oak]] from the ''Pokémon'' franchise. The reason behind the change is unknown. *The Catacombs was intended to have {{Green|10}} floors, with {{MobSprite|Maxor}} in Floor 7, {{MobSprite|Goldor}} in Floor 8, {{MobSprite|Storm}} in Floor 9, and {{MobSprite|Necron}} in Floor 10.
